initial_patch.sample: The 56 quads failing the Rust post-optimizer orientation check
initial_patch.method: Dot of quad area vector with average assigned-source normals, not the stricter per-triangle final orientation gate.

alternative_initialization.change: Only initial output positions replaced by the arithmetic mean of existing source-member positions. All source samples, normals, directions, memberships, quad indices, ideal edge vectors and flags unchanged.

quality.note: Distance measurements use topology-only render diagonals; these are diagnostics, not acceptance or a self-intersection test.

alternative_initialization.conclusion: Fingertip coverage improves but the reversed patch remains; initialization alone does not solve the problem.

edge_target_diagnostic.method: Length of sum of four initial ideal-edge vectors divided by their total length. Descriptive correlation, not proof of cause.

interpretation: Both pinned original positioning stages reproduce the problem with the same earlier data.
The normalized-axis upstream variant matches Rust to 2.01e-10 model units on this current case.
The earlier field/integer mapping and its derived geometric constraints are now the primary investigation; a particular defect in those stages has not yet been established.
No runtime algorithm, acceptance threshold or app integration changed in this experiment.
